product_from_film: Runable 2.0 is an AI workspace for planning and making slides, websites, media and agents from prompts.
explains_well: One restaurant expansion brief leads to a site, partner deck, promo video and social carousel, making the range of outputs concrete.
unclear: The booking example stops at a request to the voice interface; it does not show a confirmed reservation or the resulting booking record.
scenario: A founder introduces planning and editing controls, then uses a restaurant launch to connect several outputs.
product_clear_basis: The ASR draft names slides and full-stack websites around 12–19s; later product screens demonstrate these output types.

sound.detail: The ASR draft coherently introduces the release, planning, editing, rollback, forks, canvas and restaurant outputs. It also transcribes a booking greeting and request, but no confirmed reservation. Some opening timing and brief/model-name words are uncertain; no delivery, music, effects, latency or synchronization was heard or verified.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V10; script names features and connects output screens.
sound.evidence: 306-speech.json draft plus visible captions; not validated listening.

categories.finding: Release introduction → plan/edit controls → one restaurant brief with several outputs → booking interface → creative examples.
A logo and named founder open the film, followed by an adoption claim.
Builders and creators needing sites, decks and media are named in the draft and illustrated in the UI.
Cursor and interface state changes show planning, approval, deck editing, rollback and branching. Exact animation mechanics are unverified.
The output list repeatedly returns between restaurant artifacts, giving the sequence a clear navigation anchor.
White founder and workspace views are interrupted by red pizza branding, dark slides and pale glossy imagery.
Feature pills and captions help orientation; dense plans, task lists and decks need closer reading than the wide view offers.
ASR supports a founder-led explanation and booking exchange. Delivery and actual voice-agent timing are unknown.

categories.finding: Planning and output types are visually legible, but some broad capability claims rely on the draft.
The repeated output list and consistent pizza subject guide attention through otherwise different formats.
About 45s introduce the release before controls are demonstrated; the restaurant example occupies roughly 47s.
The restaurant brief pays off in several visible artifacts; the booking request has no final result.
The maker presentation suggests confidence and the artifact range suggests possibility; viewer response is not measured.
The second-location scenario gives site, deck, video and carousel a common purpose.
Adoption, benchmark, speed and functional claims are not independently verified. A waveform and request do not prove booking completion.
Plan approval, rollback and chat forks make user control more specific than a simple one-prompt promise.
Finish the reservation example with a visible result.
